title: Is Array a Preorder of Some ‌Binary Tree
summary: Given a 0-indexed integer 2D array nodes, determine if the array represents the preorder traversal of some binary tree.
statement: Given a 0-indexed integer 2D array nodes, determine if the array represents the preorder traversal of some binary tree. Each node is defined by [id, parentId], where id is the node's identifier and parentId is the identifier of its parent (or -1 if it has no parent). Return true if the array is a valid preorder traversal, otherwise return false.
constraints: Each pair is [node,parent], with parent -1 only for the root.
Determine whether the listed node order can be a preorder traversal of the described rooted binary tree.
Return false when a parent is not an active ancestor at its child’s position.
hints: Preorder keeps the current root-to-node ancestor path.
Maintain that path as a stack.
Before a non-root node, pop completed subtrees until its parent is on top; fail if absent.
A node may appear next exactly when its parent remains an active ancestor, which the stack represents.
editorial: A node may appear next exactly when its parent remains an active ancestor, which the stack represents.

tests.explanation: After finishing node one, preorder returns to root zero before entering node two and its children.
Node four names two as parent after traversal already left two, so the order is invalid.
